description: Build and test a structural equation model: specify the path diagram, translate to equations, estimate parameters, assess fit, test modifications, compare nested models, and produce the SEM report.

steps.description: Specify the theoretical model as a path diagram with latent variables, observed indicators, and hypothesized causal paths.

inputs.name: research-question
inputs.desc: The causal or measurement question the model addresses

inputs.name: variable-list
inputs.desc: All observed and latent variables with their roles

outputs.name: path-diagram
outputs.desc: The specified path diagram with all paths labeled

outputs.name: model-hypotheses
outputs.desc: Each path stated as a testable directional hypothesis

process: List all latent constructs and their observed indicator variables.
Draw directed paths for hypothesized causal relationships and covariance arcs for correlated errors.
Label each path with a parameter name and document the theoretical justification.
Check identification rules: count free parameters against known elements.

steps.description: Translate the path diagram into a system of structural and measurement equations ready for estimation software.

inputs.name: path-diagram
inputs.desc: The specified path diagram with labeled paths

outputs.name: equation-system
outputs.desc: Structural and measurement equations in matrix notation

outputs.name: software-syntax
outputs.desc: Model syntax for the estimation software (lavaan, Mplus, or AMOS)

process: Write the measurement model equations linking latent variables to their indicators.
Write the structural equations linking latent variables to each other.
Set scale for each latent variable by fixing one loading or the variance.
Export to software syntax with proper constraints and free parameters.

steps.description: Estimate model parameters using maximum likelihood, weighted least squares, or robust variants appropriate to the data.

inputs.name: software-syntax
inputs.desc: Model syntax for the estimation software

inputs.name: dataset
inputs.desc: Covariance matrix or raw data with sample size

outputs.name: parameter-estimates
outputs.desc: Point estimates, standard errors, and p-values for all free parameters

outputs.name: estimation-diagnostics
outputs.desc: Convergence status, improper solutions, and Heywood cases

process: Select the estimator based on data properties (ML for continuous normal, WLSMV for categorical, MLR for non-normal).
Run the estimation and check for convergence.
Flag any negative variances, correlations above 1.0, or non-positive-definite matrices.
Record standardized and unstandardized solutions.

steps.description: Assess how well the estimated model reproduces the observed data using standard fit indices.

outputs.name: fit-indices
outputs.desc: Chi-square, CFI, TLI, RMSEA with 90% CI, SRMR, AIC, BIC

outputs.name: fit-verdict
outputs.desc: Pass, marginal, or fail against conventional thresholds

process: Compute absolute fit indices: chi-square, SRMR.
Compute incremental fit indices: CFI, TLI against the null model.
Compute parsimony-corrected indices: RMSEA with confidence interval, AIC, BIC.
Compare each index against conventional cutoffs (CFI > 0.95, RMSEA < 0.06, SRMR < 0.08) and note marginal cases.

steps.description: Examine modification indices to identify potential model improvements, applied only where theoretically justified.

outputs.name: modification-indices
outputs.desc: Ranked list of freed parameters with expected chi-square drop

outputs.name: respecification-candidates
outputs.desc: Theoretically defensible modifications with expected fit improvement

process: Extract modification indices for all fixed parameters.
Rank by expected parameter change and chi-square improvement.
Filter to retain only those with theoretical justification.
Document the rationale for each candidate modification.

steps.description: Compare the specified model against nested alternatives to test whether added complexity is warranted.

inputs.name: fit-indices
inputs.desc: Fit indices from the original model

outputs.name: model-comparison-table
outputs.desc: Chi-square difference tests, AIC, BIC for each nested pair

outputs.name: best-model
outputs.desc: The selected model with justification

process: Estimate each candidate respecified model.
Compute chi-square difference tests (Satorra-Bentler scaled if using robust estimator).
Compare AIC and BIC across all candidates and the original.
Select the model that balances fit improvement against parsimony.

steps.description: Produce the SEM report with path diagram, fit indices, parameter table, and interpretation.

outputs.name: sem-report
outputs.desc: The full SEM analysis report

outputs.name: path-diagram-final
outputs.desc: Annotated path diagram with standardized estimates

process: Draw the final path diagram with standardized estimates on each path.
Write the parameter table with estimates, standard errors, p-values, and standardized values.
Summarize which hypotheses were supported and which were not.
Note limitations: sample size adequacy, normality assumptions, cross-sectional design constraints.

description: Quantify proteins from mass spectrometry data: import raw files, search the database, filter by FDR, normalize, run differential expression, perform pathway enrichment, and produce the report.

steps.description: Import and inspect raw mass spectrometry files, checking acquisition quality before processing.

inputs.name: acquisition-metadata
inputs.desc: Instrument settings, sample labels, and run order

outputs.name: imported-spectra
outputs.desc: Parsed spectra ready for database search

outputs.name: quality-summary
outputs.desc: Total spectra, MS2 count, injection time distribution, TIC plots

process: Parse each raw file and extract MS1 and MS2 spectra.
Generate total ion chromatograms and base peak chromatograms for visual QC.
Check spray stability, retention time alignment, and injection replicates.
Flag runs with anomalous TIC profiles or low MS2 counts.

steps.description: Search MS2 spectra against a protein sequence database to identify peptides and infer proteins.

inputs.name: protein-database
inputs.desc: FASTA file of target and decoy protein sequences

outputs.name: peptide-spectrum-matches
outputs.desc: All PSMs with scores and decoy labels

outputs.name: search-parameters
outputs.desc: Enzyme, mass tolerance, modifications, and other search settings

process: Configure the search engine with enzyme specificity, mass tolerance, and variable modifications.
Append a decoy database (reversed or shuffled sequences) for FDR estimation.
Run the search and score each peptide-spectrum match.
Record all PSMs with their scores, delta scores, and decoy flags.

steps.description: Filter peptide and protein identifications to a target false discovery rate using the target-decoy approach.

inputs.name: peptide-spectrum-matches
inputs.desc: All PSMs with scores and decoy labels

inputs.name: fdr-threshold
inputs.desc: Target FDR (typically 0.01 at peptide and protein level)

outputs.name: filtered-peptides
outputs.desc: Peptides passing the FDR threshold

outputs.name: protein-groups
outputs.desc: Inferred protein groups with parsimony applied

process: Sort PSMs by score and compute the FDR at each score threshold using target-decoy counting.
Apply the peptide-level FDR cutoff.
Infer protein groups using the principle of parsimony (Occam's razor).
Apply protein-level FDR filtering.

steps.description: Normalize protein abundances across samples to correct for systematic technical variation.

inputs.name: experimental-design
inputs.desc: Sample groups, batches, and biological replicates

outputs.name: normalized-abundances
outputs.desc: Protein abundance matrix after normalization

outputs.name: normalization-report
outputs.desc: Before and after distributions, method used, and batch effects assessed

process: Log-transform intensity values.
Select normalization method (median centering, quantile, or variance stabilization).
Apply normalization and check for residual batch effects using PCA or clustering.
Impute remaining missing values using appropriate strategy (MinProb, KNN, or left-censored).

steps.description: Test for differentially expressed proteins between experimental conditions.

outputs.name: de-results
outputs.desc: Proteins with fold change, p-value, and adjusted p-value

outputs.name: volcano-plot-data
outputs.desc: Data for volcano plot visualization

process: Fit a linear model for each protein with condition as the main factor.
Apply empirical Bayes moderation of variance (limma-style).
Correct for multiple testing using Benjamini-Hochberg FDR.
Flag proteins meeting both fold-change and adjusted p-value thresholds.

steps.description: Test whether differentially expressed proteins cluster in known biological pathways or functional categories.

inputs.name: de-results
inputs.desc: Differential expression results with gene/protein identifiers

inputs.name: pathway-database
inputs.desc: Gene ontology, KEGG, Reactome, or custom pathway annotations

outputs.name: enrichment-results
outputs.desc: Enriched pathways with p-values and gene counts

outputs.name: pathway-visualization
outputs.desc: Network or bar plot of top enriched terms

process: Map protein identifiers to gene symbols for annotation lookup.
Run over-representation analysis or gene set enrichment analysis.
Correct enrichment p-values for multiple testing.
Visualize top enriched terms and their member proteins.

steps.description: Produce the proteomics analysis report with methods, QC, differential results, and pathway findings.

outputs.name: proteomics-report
outputs.desc: The full proteomics analysis report

outputs.name: supplementary-tables
outputs.desc: Complete protein list, DE table, and enrichment table

process: Summarize the experimental design and number of identifications at each filtering stage.
Present the top differentially expressed proteins with volcano and heatmap visualizations.
Present enriched pathways with biological interpretation.
List all software versions, parameters, and databases used for reproducibility.

description: Analyze soil samples: prepare the sample, measure physical, chemical, and biological properties, interpret for land use suitability, and produce the soil report.

steps.description: Prepare soil samples for laboratory analysis following standard protocols.

inputs.name: field-samples
inputs.desc: Raw soil samples with collection metadata (location, depth, date)

inputs.name: analysis-plan
inputs.desc: Which tests will be run and their preparation requirements

outputs.name: prepared-samples
outputs.desc: Air-dried, sieved, and split samples ready for each test

outputs.name: prep-log
outputs.desc: Record of preparation steps, weights, and any anomalies

process: Air-dry samples at room temperature, noting initial moisture content.
Remove roots, stones, and debris, then sieve through 2mm mesh.
Split into aliquots for physical, chemical, and biological analyses.
Record sample weights and store biological aliquots at appropriate temperature.

steps.description: Measure soil physical properties: texture, bulk density, and water holding capacity.

inputs.name: prepared-samples
inputs.desc: Sieved soil samples ready for physical testing

inputs.name: field-bulk-density-cores
inputs.desc: Intact cores for bulk density measurement

outputs.name: physical-results
outputs.desc: Texture class, bulk density, porosity, and water holding capacity

outputs.name: texture-triangle-position
outputs.desc: Sand/silt/clay percentages plotted on the texture triangle

process: Determine particle size distribution by hydrometer or pipette method.
Classify texture using the USDA texture triangle.
Measure bulk density from intact core weight and volume.
Determine water holding capacity at field capacity and permanent wilting point.

steps.description: Measure soil chemical properties: pH, cation exchange capacity, organic matter, and nutrient levels.

inputs.name: prepared-samples
inputs.desc: Sieved soil samples ready for chemical testing

outputs.name: chemical-results
outputs.desc: pH, CEC, organic matter percentage, and nutrient concentrations

outputs.name: nutrient-status
outputs.desc: Nutrient levels rated as deficient, adequate, or excessive

process: Measure pH in water and CaCl2 solution.
Determine organic matter by loss-on-ignition or Walkley-Black method.
Measure cation exchange capacity by ammonium acetate extraction.
Extract and quantify available nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium.

steps.description: Measure soil biological activity: microbial biomass and soil respiration.

inputs.name: prepared-samples
inputs.desc: Fresh (not dried) soil aliquots for biological testing

outputs.name: biological-results
outputs.desc: Microbial biomass carbon, soil respiration rate, and metabolic quotient

outputs.name: biological-health-rating
outputs.desc: Biological activity rated relative to reference values for the soil type

process: Measure microbial biomass carbon by chloroform fumigation-extraction.
Measure basal soil respiration by CO2 evolution over 24 hours.
Calculate the metabolic quotient (qCO2) as respiration per unit biomass.
Compare results against reference values for the climate zone and soil type.

steps.description: Interpret the combined physical, chemical, and biological results for land use suitability.

outputs.name: suitability-assessment
outputs.desc: Land use suitability ratings for agriculture, construction, and conservation

outputs.name: amendment-recommendations
outputs.desc: Specific soil amendments with application rates to address deficiencies

process: Score each property against standard suitability criteria for the intended land use.
Identify limiting factors (drainage, acidity, nutrient deficiency, compaction).
Recommend amendments with rates (lime, fertilizer, organic matter, gypsum).
Rate overall suitability as high, moderate, low, or unsuitable with the primary constraints listed.

steps.description: Produce the soil analysis report with all measurements, interpretations, and recommendations.

outputs.name: soil-report
outputs.desc: The full soil analysis report

outputs.name: data-tables
outputs.desc: Summary tables of all measured properties

process: Compile all measurements into summary tables with units and reference ranges.
Write the interpretation section explaining what each result means for the site.
Present amendment recommendations with expected outcomes and costs.
Include methods, lab accreditation, and quality control results.

description: Analyze acoustic recordings: import audio, generate spectrograms, detect and classify events, extract features, compute activity indices, and produce the report.

steps.description: Import acoustic recordings and inspect their technical quality before analysis.

inputs.name: audio-files
inputs.desc: WAV or FLAC recordings with collection metadata

inputs.name: deployment-log
inputs.desc: Recorder locations, dates, gain settings, and duty cycle

outputs.name: validated-recordings
outputs.desc: Recordings passing quality checks with metadata attached

outputs.name: quality-flags
outputs.desc: Recordings flagged for clipping, low SNR, or equipment noise

process: Read file headers and verify sample rate, bit depth, and duration match the deployment log.
Scan for clipping, DC offset, and abnormal amplitude distributions.
Check for recorder self-noise, wind contamination, or rain masking.
Tag each file with its location, date, time, and quality status.

steps.description: Generate spectrograms from validated recordings for visual inspection and automated detection.

outputs.name: spectrograms
outputs.desc: Time-frequency representations of each recording segment

outputs.name: spectrogram-parameters
outputs.desc: FFT size, window type, overlap, and frequency range used

process: Select FFT parameters based on target frequency range and time resolution.
Compute short-time Fourier transforms for each recording.
Apply noise floor estimation and spectral subtraction if needed.
Store spectrograms as images or arrays for downstream detection.

steps.description: Detect acoustic events of interest (animal calls, machinery, environmental sounds) in the spectrograms.

inputs.name: target-species-templates
inputs.desc: Reference spectrograms or model weights for target sounds

outputs.name: detected-events
outputs.desc: List of detections with start time, end time, frequency range, and confidence score

outputs.name: detection-summary
outputs.desc: Total detections per class per recording

process: Run the detector (template matching, energy threshold, or trained classifier) across all spectrograms.
Apply confidence threshold to retain high-quality detections.
Merge overlapping detections of the same class.
Manual-review a random subset to estimate precision and recall.

steps.description: Extract quantitative acoustic features from each detected event for downstream analysis.

inputs.name: detected-events
inputs.desc: Detected sound events with time and frequency bounds

outputs.name: acoustic-features
outputs.desc: Feature table with frequency, duration, bandwidth, modulation rate, and SNR per event

outputs.name: feature-distributions
outputs.desc: Summary statistics and histograms for each feature

process: Extract each event's audio segment.
Measure peak frequency, bandwidth, duration, inter-onset interval, and frequency modulation rate.
Compute signal-to-noise ratio relative to the surrounding background.
Compile all features into a structured table indexed by event ID.

steps.description: Compute acoustic indices and occupancy estimates to characterize overall soundscape activity.

outputs.name: acoustic-indices
outputs.desc: ACI, bioacoustic index, NDSI, and species-specific occupancy estimates

outputs.name: temporal-patterns
outputs.desc: Diel and seasonal activity patterns per species or sound class

process: Compute landscape-level indices (ACI, H, NDSI) per time bin.
Estimate single-season occupancy for target species accounting for imperfect detection.
Plot diel activity patterns (detections per hour across the 24-hour cycle).
Plot seasonal trends if multi-month data are available.

steps.description: Produce the acoustic analysis report with methods, detections, indices, and ecological interpretation.

inputs.name: acoustic-indices
inputs.desc: Computed acoustic indices and occupancy estimates

outputs.name: acoustic-report
outputs.desc: The full acoustic analysis report

outputs.name: detection-database
outputs.desc: Complete database of all detections with features and classifications

process: Summarize survey effort (recorder-hours, spatial coverage).
Present species detection results with occupancy estimates and confidence intervals.
Interpret acoustic indices in the context of habitat quality and disturbance.
Document detector performance, limitations, and recommendations for future surveys.

description: Run a genetic association study (GWAS): load phenotype and genotype data, perform QC, correct for population stratification, test associations, adjust for multiple testing, and produce the report.

steps.description: Load and align phenotype and genotype datasets, verifying sample overlap and data formats.

inputs.name: genotype-files
inputs.desc: Genotype data in PLINK, VCF, or BGEN format

inputs.name: phenotype-file
inputs.desc: Phenotype and covariate data with sample identifiers

outputs.name: aligned-dataset
outputs.desc: Matched genotype-phenotype dataset ready for QC

outputs.name: sample-summary
outputs.desc: Sample count, phenotype distribution, and missing data rates

process: Read genotype and phenotype files and match on sample identifiers.
Report the number of overlapping samples and any ID mismatches.
Summarize the phenotype distribution (continuous: mean, SD; binary: case/control counts).
List available covariates (age, sex, principal components).

steps.description: Filter samples and variants that fail quality thresholds before association testing.

outputs.name: qc-passed-dataset
outputs.desc: Dataset with failing samples and variants removed

outputs.name: qc-report
outputs.desc: Number removed at each step and the applied thresholds

process: Remove samples with genotyping rate below threshold (typically 0.98) or sex mismatches.
Remove variants with call rate below threshold, minor allele frequency below cutoff, or Hardy-Weinberg p-value below threshold in controls.
Check for cryptic relatedness and remove one from each related pair (IBD > 0.185).
Record the count removed at each step.

steps.description: Compute principal components from the genotype data to correct for population stratification.

outputs.name: principal-components
outputs.desc: Top principal components (typically 10-20) per sample

outputs.name: population-structure-plot
outputs.desc: PC1 vs PC2 scatter plot colored by self-reported ancestry

process: Prune variants for linkage disequilibrium to get an independent set.
Compute the genomic relationship matrix and extract principal components.
Plot PC1 vs PC2 and compare with known reference populations.
Select the number of PCs to include as covariates (scree plot or Tracy-Widom test).

steps.description: Test each variant for association with the phenotype, adjusting for covariates and principal components.

outputs.name: association-results
outputs.desc: Per-variant test statistics: beta, SE, p-value, allele frequency

outputs.name: genomic-inflation
outputs.desc: Lambda GC (genomic inflation factor) and QQ plot

process: Select the regression model (linear for continuous, logistic for binary phenotype).
Include covariates: age, sex, and selected principal components.
Run the association test across all QC-passed variants.
Compute the genomic inflation factor and generate the QQ plot to check for residual confounding.

steps.description: Adjust association p-values for the large number of tests performed.

outputs.name: adjusted-results
outputs.desc: Variants with genome-wide significance flag and FDR q-values

outputs.name: manhattan-plot-data
outputs.desc: Data for Manhattan plot with significance thresholds marked

process: Apply genome-wide significance threshold (5e-8 for common GWAS).
Compute Benjamini-Hochberg FDR q-values for a suggestive tier.
Identify independent lead SNPs by clumping in LD windows.
Prepare Manhattan plot data with chromosome positions and negative log p-values.

steps.description: Annotate and interpret genome-wide significant hits in their biological context.

inputs.name: adjusted-results
inputs.desc: Significant and suggestive variants with positions

outputs.name: annotated-hits
outputs.desc: Significant loci with nearest genes, eQTL data, and known associations

outputs.name: biological-interpretation
outputs.desc: Summary of implicated pathways and candidate causal genes

process: Map each lead SNP to its genomic context (nearest gene, coding consequence, regulatory annotations).
Cross-reference with eQTL databases (GTEx) to identify genes whose expression is affected.
Check the GWAS catalog for prior associations at the same loci.
Summarize the biological story: which pathways and tissues are implicated.

steps.description: Produce the GWAS report with Manhattan plot, QQ plot, hit table, and biological interpretation.

outputs.name: gwas-report
outputs.desc: The full GWAS analysis report

outputs.name: summary-statistics-file
outputs.desc: Complete summary statistics for public deposition

process: Present Manhattan and QQ plots with the genomic inflation factor.
Table all genome-wide significant loci with effect sizes, frequencies, and annotations.
Interpret findings in the context of known biology and prior GWAS.
Document software, versions, and parameters for reproducibility.

description: Analyze a sediment core: log the core, subsample, measure organic content and grain size, identify microfossils, build the age model, and reconstruct the paleoenvironment.

steps.description: Log the sediment core with visual description, photography, and non-destructive measurements.

inputs.name: core-sections
inputs.desc: Split core halves with depth markings

inputs.name: site-metadata
inputs.desc: Coring location, water depth, and collection method

outputs.name: core-log
outputs.desc: Visual description, color (Munsell), texture, and boundaries at each depth

outputs.name: core-photos
outputs.desc: High-resolution photographs of each section

process: Photograph each section under consistent lighting with a color card and ruler.
Describe sediment color using Munsell charts, texture, visible structures, and fossil content.
Mark lithological boundaries and note any disturbance from coring.
Run non-destructive scans (magnetic susceptibility, XRF core scanning) if available.

steps.description: Subsample the core at defined intervals for destructive analyses.

inputs.name: sampling-plan
inputs.desc: Depth intervals and volume required for each analysis

outputs.name: subsamples
outputs.desc: Labeled samples at each depth with recorded wet weight

outputs.name: sampling-log
outputs.desc: Exact depths, volumes, and any gaps or disturbance noted

process: Mark sampling positions at the planned interval (typically 1cm or 0.5cm).
Extract each subsample using a clean spatula or syringe cutter.
Record wet weight and split into aliquots for LOI, grain size, microfossils, and dating.
Store dating aliquots separately to avoid contamination.

steps.description: Measure organic and carbonate content by loss-on-ignition at two temperatures.

inputs.name: subsamples
inputs.desc: Dried and weighed subsamples at each depth

outputs.name: loi-results
outputs.desc: Organic matter (550C) and carbonate (950C) percentages per depth

outputs.name: loi-profile
outputs.desc: Downcore plot of organic and carbonate content

process: Dry subsamples at 105C overnight and record dry weight.
Combust at 550C for 4 hours and record weight loss (organic matter).
Combust at 950C for 2 hours and record further weight loss (carbonate).
Calculate percentages and plot the downcore profiles.

steps.description: Measure grain size distribution at each depth to infer depositional energy.

outputs.name: grain-size-results
outputs.desc: Percentage sand, silt, clay and statistical parameters (mean, sorting, skewness) per depth

outputs.name: grain-size-profile
outputs.desc: Downcore plot of grain size fractions

process: Remove organic matter with hydrogen peroxide and disperse with sodium hexametaphosphate.
Measure particle size distribution by laser diffraction or sieve-pipette method.
Calculate statistical parameters: mean grain size, sorting, skewness.
Plot downcore profiles and interpret in terms of depositional energy changes.

steps.description: Identify and count microfossils (pollen, diatoms, foraminifera, or ostracods) at selected depths.

inputs.name: reference-collection
inputs.desc: Identification keys or atlas for the target microfossil group

outputs.name: microfossil-counts
outputs.desc: Counts of each taxon per depth with total counted

outputs.name: assemblage-diagram
outputs.desc: Percentage or concentration diagram of key taxa through the core

process: Process subsamples using the appropriate chemical preparation (acetolysis for pollen, acid cleaning for diatoms).
Mount on slides and count a minimum of 300 specimens per sample (or equivalent counting sum).
Identify to the lowest practical taxonomic level using the reference collection.
Calculate percentages or concentrations and plot the assemblage diagram.

steps.description: Build the age-depth model from radiocarbon dates, lead-210, or other chronological markers.

inputs.name: dating-results
inputs.desc: Radiocarbon ages, Pb-210 activities, or tephra identifications with depths

inputs.name: core-log
inputs.desc: Visual log noting any hiatuses or disturbed sections

outputs.name: age-model
outputs.desc: Age-depth relationship with uncertainty envelope

outputs.name: sedimentation-rates
outputs.desc: Accumulation rates (cm/yr or g/cm2/yr) through the core

process: Calibrate radiocarbon ages using the appropriate curve (IntCal, SHCal, or Marine).
Exclude dates from reworked material or known contaminants.
Build the age-depth model using Bayesian methods (Bacon, OxCal, or rbacon).
Extract sedimentation rates and their uncertainties for each interval.

steps.description: Reconstruct paleoenvironmental conditions by combining all proxy data on the age model.

outputs.name: paleoenvironment-reconstruction
outputs.desc: Narrative and quantitative reconstruction of past environmental conditions through time

outputs.name: summary-diagram
outputs.desc: Multi-proxy summary diagram plotted against the age model

process: Plot all proxies on the common age scale.
Identify zones of similar proxy behavior using constrained cluster analysis (CONISS).
Apply transfer functions to microfossil data if calibration datasets are available.
Write the paleoenvironmental narrative for each zone, noting cause-and-effect relationships between proxies.

description: Model a chemical reaction system: write rate equations, estimate rate constants, integrate numerically, validate against measurements, test sensitivity, and produce the report.

steps.description: Write the system of ordinary differential equations describing the proposed reaction mechanism.

inputs.name: species-list
inputs.desc: All chemical species involved (reactants, intermediates, products)

outputs.name: ode-system
outputs.desc: Rate equations (dC/dt) for each species

outputs.name: parameter-list
outputs.desc: Rate constants to be estimated with their units

process: For each species, sum the contribution from every elementary reaction it appears in.
Apply the law of mass action to write the rate expression for each elementary step.
Check stoichiometric consistency: total atoms must balance in each equation.
List all rate constants as free parameters with expected order of magnitude.

steps.description: Estimate rate constants by fitting the ODE system to experimental concentration-time data.

inputs.name: experimental-data
inputs.desc: Measured concentrations of observable species over time

outputs.name: estimated-constants
outputs.desc: Best-fit rate constants with confidence intervals

outputs.name: fit-quality
outputs.desc: Residuals, R-squared, and parameter correlation matrix

process: Set initial guesses from literature or Arrhenius estimates.
Minimize the sum of squared residuals between model predictions and data using Levenberg-Marquardt or differential evolution.
Compute confidence intervals from the Hessian or by bootstrapping.
Check for parameter identifiability: flag constants whose confidence intervals span orders of magnitude.

steps.description: Numerically integrate the ODE system to produce concentration-time profiles for all species.

outputs.name: concentration-profiles
outputs.desc: Time-resolved concentrations for all species

outputs.name: integration-diagnostics
outputs.desc: Solver step size, stiffness flags, and mass conservation check

process: Select the integrator based on stiffness (explicit for non-stiff, BDF or Radau for stiff systems).
Set absolute and relative tolerances tight enough for the required precision.
Integrate and check mass conservation at each output time.
Flag any negative concentrations or solver failures.

steps.description: Compare model predictions against experimental data to validate the mechanism.

outputs.name: validation-results
outputs.desc: Residual plots, RMSE per species, and systematic deviation assessment

outputs.name: model-adequacy-verdict
outputs.desc: Pass or fail with identified problem regions

process: Overlay model predictions on experimental data for each observable species.
Compute residuals and check for systematic patterns (not just magnitude).
Test against data not used in fitting (holdout validation) if available.
Identify time windows or species where the model deviates, suggesting missing reactions.

steps.description: Determine which rate constants most influence the model output.

outputs.name: sensitivity-coefficients
outputs.desc: Normalized sensitivity of each species to each rate constant over time

outputs.name: parameter-ranking
outputs.desc: Rate constants ranked by influence on the key observable

process: Compute local sensitivity coefficients by perturbing each rate constant by a small fraction.
Normalize sensitivities to make them comparable across parameters with different magnitudes.
Identify the dominant rate constants at early, intermediate, and late times.
Highlight parameters that are both influential and poorly constrained.

steps.description: Compare the proposed mechanism against one or more alternative mechanisms.

inputs.name: validation-results
inputs.desc: Fit quality for the current mechanism

outputs.name: mechanism-comparison
outputs.desc: AIC, BIC, and residual comparison across mechanisms

outputs.name: best-mechanism
outputs.desc: The selected mechanism with justification

process: Fit each alternative mechanism to the same experimental data.
Compare using AIC and BIC to penalize for additional parameters.
Check whether the alternative resolves systematic deviations identified in validation.
Select the mechanism that best balances fit quality and parsimony.

steps.description: Produce the chemical kinetics report with the mechanism, fitted constants, validation, and sensitivity results.

outputs.name: kinetics-report
outputs.desc: The full kinetics modeling report

outputs.name: model-files
outputs.desc: ODE system, fitted parameters, and integration scripts for reproducibility

process: Present the reaction mechanism, rate equations, and estimated constants with uncertainties.
Show model-data overlays and residual analysis.
Summarize sensitivity analysis and which parameters need tighter experimental constraints.
Provide the computational files for others to reproduce the results.

description: Classify land cover from remote sensing imagery: preprocess, sample, select features, train, validate, and produce the classified map.

steps.description: Preprocess satellite or aerial imagery: atmospheric correction, co-registration, and cloud masking.

inputs.name: raw-imagery
inputs.desc: Multi-band satellite or aerial images with metadata

inputs.name: reference-data
inputs.desc: Ground control points or reference image for co-registration

outputs.name: corrected-imagery
outputs.desc: Surface reflectance images, co-registered and cloud-masked

outputs.name: preprocessing-log
outputs.desc: Atmospheric model used, RMS co-registration error, and cloud percentage

process: Apply atmospheric correction to convert DN to surface reflectance (6S, FLAASH, or Sen2Cor).
Co-register to the reference using ground control points or automated feature matching.
Generate and apply a cloud and cloud shadow mask.
Compute spectral indices (NDVI, NDWI, NDBI) and add as additional bands.

steps.description: Collect training and validation samples for the land cover classes of interest.

inputs.name: class-definitions
inputs.desc: Target land cover classes with descriptions and examples

outputs.name: training-samples
outputs.desc: Labeled pixel locations with class assignments

outputs.name: validation-samples
outputs.desc: Independent labeled pixels reserved for accuracy assessment

process: Define the classification scheme with clear, mutually exclusive class definitions.
Collect training polygons from field visits, very-high-resolution imagery, or existing maps.
Split samples into training (70%) and validation (30%) ensuring spatial separation.
Check class balance and augment under-represented classes if needed.

steps.description: Select the most discriminating features from spectral bands, indices, and texture measures.

outputs.name: selected-features
outputs.desc: Ranked feature set with importance scores

outputs.name: feature-space-visualization
outputs.desc: Scatter plots of top features colored by class

process: Extract pixel values for all bands, indices, and texture measures at training locations.
Compute feature importance using random forest variable importance or mutual information.
Remove highly correlated features (correlation > 0.95) keeping the more important one.
Visualize the top features in 2D scatter plots to check class separability.

steps.description: Train the land cover classifier on the selected features and training samples.

inputs.name: selected-features
inputs.desc: Feature set to use for classification

outputs.name: trained-classifier
outputs.desc: Fitted classification model with parameters

outputs.name: training-accuracy
outputs.desc: Cross-validated accuracy on training data

process: Select the classifier algorithm (random forest, SVM, or gradient boosting).
Tune hyperparameters using cross-validation on the training set.
Train the final model on all training samples with optimal hyperparameters.
Record out-of-bag or cross-validation accuracy as an initial performance estimate.

steps.description: Validate the classifier against the independent validation samples and compute accuracy metrics.

outputs.name: confusion-matrix
outputs.desc: Full confusion matrix with per-class producer and user accuracy

outputs.name: accuracy-metrics
outputs.desc: Overall accuracy, kappa coefficient, and F1 per class

process: Predict classes for all validation sample locations.
Build the confusion matrix comparing predicted vs reference classes.
Compute overall accuracy, Cohen's kappa, and per-class producer/user accuracy and F1.
Identify classes with poor accuracy and assess whether more training data or class merging is needed.

steps.description: Apply the trained classifier to the full image and produce the final land cover map.

outputs.name: classified-map
outputs.desc: Raster land cover map with class labels and legend

outputs.name: classification-report
outputs.desc: Methods, accuracy assessment, and area estimates per class

process: Apply the classifier to every pixel in the image extent.
Apply post-classification filtering (minimum mapping unit, majority filter) to reduce salt-and-pepper noise.
Compute area estimates per class with confidence intervals adjusted for classification error.
Export the map as a GeoTIFF with proper projection, legend, and metadata.

description: Assess water quality: collect samples, measure physical, chemical, and biological parameters, compare against standards, and produce the report.

steps.description: Collect water samples following standard protocols appropriate to the parameters being measured.

inputs.name: sampling-plan
inputs.desc: Locations, depths, frequencies, and parameters to measure

outputs.name: collected-samples
outputs.desc: Water samples in appropriate containers with preservatives applied

outputs.name: field-log
outputs.desc: Collection times, conditions, in-situ measurements, and chain of custody

process: Prepare bottles with appropriate preservatives for each analyte group.
Collect samples at specified depth, avoiding surface film and bottom sediment disturbance.
Record in-situ measurements (temperature, dissolved oxygen, pH, conductivity) with calibrated probes.
Label, cool to 4C, and transport to the lab within holding time.

steps.description: Measure physical water quality parameters: temperature, turbidity, conductivity, and color.

outputs.name: physical-results
outputs.desc: Temperature, turbidity (NTU), conductivity (uS/cm), TDS, and true color

outputs.name: physical-status
outputs.desc: Each parameter rated against applicable standards

process: Record temperature from field measurement (within 15 minutes of collection).
Measure turbidity by nephelometry.
Measure specific conductance at 25C and calculate total dissolved solids.
Measure true color on a filtered sample.

steps.description: Measure chemical water quality parameters: dissolved oxygen, nutrients, metals, and pH.

outputs.name: chemical-results
outputs.desc: DO, BOD, COD, pH, alkalinity, nitrate, phosphate, ammonia, and metals concentrations

outputs.name: chemical-status
outputs.desc: Each parameter rated against applicable standards

process: Measure dissolved oxygen by Winkler titration or optical sensor.
Measure BOD5 by the 5-day incubation method and COD by dichromate digestion.
Analyze nutrients (nitrate, ammonia, total phosphorus) by colorimetry or ion chromatography.
Analyze metals by ICP-MS or ICP-OES after acid digestion.

steps.description: Measure biological indicators of water quality: fecal coliform, chlorophyll-a, and benthic index.

outputs.name: biological-results
outputs.desc: Fecal coliform (CFU/100mL), E. coli, chlorophyll-a (ug/L), and benthic index score

outputs.name: biological-status
outputs.desc: Each indicator rated against applicable standards

process: Enumerate fecal coliforms and E. coli by membrane filtration.
Measure chlorophyll-a by acetone extraction and spectrophotometry.
If applicable, collect and identify benthic macroinvertebrates and compute the appropriate index (EPT ratio, BMWP, or IBI).
Rate each indicator against the applicable standard for the water body class.

steps.description: Compare all results against applicable water quality standards and identify exceedances.

outputs.name: compliance-table
outputs.desc: Each parameter compared to its standard with pass/exceed flag

outputs.name: exceedance-summary
outputs.desc: Count and severity of standard exceedances by parameter group

process: Match each parameter to the applicable standard for the water body classification.
Flag any parameter exceeding its standard, noting the magnitude of exceedance.
Classify exceedances by severity (marginal, moderate, severe).
Identify spatial or temporal patterns in exceedances.

steps.description: Produce the water quality assessment report with all results, standard comparisons, and recommendations.

outputs.name: wq-report
outputs.desc: The full water quality assessment report

outputs.name: data-tables
outputs.desc: Complete results tables with units, methods, and detection limits

process: Summarize sampling effort and conditions.
Present results by parameter group with exceedances highlighted.
Interpret likely sources of any exceedances (point source, nonpoint, natural background).
Recommend monitoring frequency adjustments or remediation actions based on findings.

description: Analyze behavioral experiment data: import trials, compute summaries, check order effects, fit the model, visualize contrasts, compute effect sizes, and produce the report.

steps.description: Import trial-level behavioral data and verify its structure against the experimental design.

inputs.name: data-files
inputs.desc: CSV or log files with one row per trial

inputs.name: design-spec
inputs.desc: Experimental factors, levels, counterbalancing scheme, and expected trial counts

outputs.name: validated-trials
outputs.desc: Trial table with all factors, responses, and timing verified

outputs.name: import-summary
outputs.desc: Subject count, trial count per condition, and missing data rate

process: Read data files and standardize column names to match the design specification.
Check that every subject has the expected number of trials per condition.
Flag trials with reaction times below 100ms (anticipatory) or above a reasonable ceiling.
Report missing data rates per subject and per condition.

steps.description: Compute summary metrics per subject per condition for use in the group-level analysis.

outputs.name: subject-summaries
outputs.desc: Mean RT, accuracy, and other metrics per subject per condition

outputs.name: outlier-report
outputs.desc: Subjects flagged for low accuracy or extreme RT distributions

process: Remove trials flagged as anticipatory or excessively slow.
Compute mean and median reaction time per subject per condition (on correct trials only).
Compute accuracy (proportion correct) per subject per condition.
Flag subjects whose overall accuracy falls below chance or whose mean RT is more than 3 SD from the group mean.

steps.description: Check for unwanted order, practice, or fatigue effects that could confound the main analysis.

inputs.name: validated-trials
inputs.desc: Trial-level data with trial number and block information

outputs.name: order-effects-report
outputs.desc: Tests for practice, fatigue, and sequence effects with p-values

outputs.name: detrended-data
outputs.desc: Data with significant order effects regressed out if needed

process: Plot RT and accuracy as a function of trial number or block to inspect for trends.
Test for a linear trend across blocks (learning/fatigue) using a regression on block number.
Test for condition-by-order interactions to check whether counterbalancing succeeded.
If significant order effects exist, decide whether to include block as a covariate or detrend.

steps.description: Fit the primary statistical model to test the experimental hypotheses.

inputs.name: subject-summaries
inputs.desc: Summary metrics per subject per condition

outputs.name: model-results
outputs.desc: ANOVA or mixed model output with F-statistics, p-values, and degrees of freedom

outputs.name: assumption-checks
outputs.desc: Normality, sphericity, and homogeneity of variance tests

process: Select the model: repeated-measures ANOVA, mixed-effects model, or Bayesian equivalent.
Check assumptions: normality of residuals (Shapiro-Wilk), sphericity (Mauchly), homogeneity of variance (Levene).
Apply corrections if assumptions are violated (Greenhouse-Geisser, robust standard errors).
Run the model and extract main effects and interactions.

steps.description: Visualize the key experimental contrasts to communicate the pattern of results.

inputs.name: model-results
inputs.desc: Statistical test results indicating which contrasts are significant

outputs.name: contrast-figures
outputs.desc: Bar or violin plots with error bars and significance annotations

outputs.name: individual-data-plots
outputs.desc: Plots showing individual subject data points alongside group means

process: Create bar or violin plots of the key conditions with within-subject error bars (Cousineau-Morey).
Overlay individual subject data points to show the distribution.
Add significance brackets for planned contrasts or post-hoc tests.
If there is an interaction, plot simple effects to decompose it.

steps.description: Compute standardized effect sizes for all significant and planned contrasts.

inputs.name: subject-summaries
inputs.desc: Summary metrics for effect size calculation

outputs.name: effect-sizes
outputs.desc: Cohen's d, partial eta-squared, or generalized eta-squared for each contrast

outputs.name: confidence-intervals
outputs.desc: 95% CIs around each effect size estimate

process: Compute partial eta-squared for omnibus ANOVA effects.
Compute Cohen's d (or dz for within-subject) for pairwise contrasts.
Compute 95% confidence intervals using non-central F or t distributions.
Compare effect sizes against benchmarks (small, medium, large) and against prior literature.

steps.description: Produce the behavioral experiment analysis report with statistics, figures, and interpretation.

outputs.name: analysis-report
outputs.desc: The full behavioral analysis report

outputs.name: statistical-supplement
outputs.desc: Complete ANOVA tables, assumption checks, and individual subject data

process: Report the sample (N, demographics, exclusions) and procedure.
Present each hypothesis with the corresponding statistical test, effect size, and figure.
Discuss whether results support, partially support, or fail to support each hypothesis.
Note limitations: sample size, generalizability, and any assumption violations.
